performance_objectives: State the characteristic features of the kingdoms and give specific examples of representative organisms.
content: Kingdom Monera (Prokaryote): single-celled, motile or non-motile organisms. No definite nucleus. Bacteria and blue-green algae make up this kingdom.
Kingdom Protista (Eukaryote): single-celled, motile or non-motile organisms. Complex cell structure with definite nucleus e.g. Chlamydomonas and Amoeba.
Kingdom Fungi (Eukaryote): mainly non-motile organisms, composed of hyphae containing nuclei e.g. moulds, mushrooms and Rhizopus.
Kingdom Plantae (Eukaryote): many-celled, non-motile organisms which contain chlorophyll that enable them to photosynthesize. Members include mosses, ferns, pines, all palms and yam plants.
Kingdom Animalia (Eukaryote): many-celled, motile organisms that feed on other organisms. Members include corals, worms, insects, snails, fishes, frogs, snakes, monkeys and cows.
